title: Squeezed state degradations due to mode mismatch and thermal aberrations in gravitational wave detectors
summary: To date, frequency-dependent squeezed light has been used to reduce quantum noise in interferometric gravitational-wave detectors by 6.1 dB (a factor of two). Future upgrades and detectors aim to both reduce quantum noise by 10 dB (a factor of three) and to increase the circulating power in the interferometer arm cavities. Achieving these goals will be extremely challenging due, in part, to the degradations to the squeezed state caused by mode mismatch between the internal interferometer optical cavities and between the auxiliary external cavities.
